## What this topic covers

This topic covers the parts of the vehicle that keep you safe and how to maintain them. It includes **grip and road-holding, brakes (and ABS, the anti-lock braking system), tires, suspension and shock absorbers, steering, and the exhaust**, plus a few **motorcycle-specific** checks. Many questions are about cause and effect, meaning what worn or wrong components do to the vehicle's behavior.

## Grip and road-holding

- **Grip (adhesion)** lets the wheels drive, steer, and hold a line. It also opposes the tire's sliding on the asphalt, whatever force pushes the tire sideways.
- Grip is **greater on rough, dry, clean** asphalt and **lower on surfaces that are wet, oily, or marked**. Anything that comes between the tire and the asphalt lowers it, leaves, ice, and mud included.
- When grip falls, the **braking distance grows** and **hard braking** becomes dangerous.
- When grip falls, the wheels can **skid**, in curves above all, and the drive wheels can **spin**.
- Where grip is low, **speed must come down**, on every kind of road and not only in curves. Low grip also caps the speed at which a curve can be taken safely.
- Grip is notably lower on **tram rails, road markings, and manhole covers when wet**, which matters for motorcycles. A motorcycle's grip depends on the **type of road surface** it is crossing.

## Curves: skidding and rollover

- In a curve a force pushes the vehicle **toward the outside**, and it **grows with speed**.
- Too much speed can cause a **skid** or a **rollover**.
- Rollover is made more likely by a **high or unsecured load**, a **narrow track** with the wheels close together, and a **tight curve** with a small radius.

## Brakes and ABS

### The three brakes

Italian law distinguishes **three brakes**. They are three braking functions, not three controls: one slows and stops the vehicle in motion, one stops it when the first fails, and one holds it still when parked. Two words describe how a brake carries its force, and the bullets below use both: a **hydraulic** brake sends it through fluid in a sealed circuit, while a **mechanical** one sends it through a rod, a cable or a linkage.

- The **service brake** (*freno di servizio*) is the foot pedal. It slows and stops the vehicle in motion, it is **hydraulic**, and it is built on **two separate circuits**, so a single failure disables only part of it.
- The **secondary brake** (*freno di soccorso*) is the braking that remains when part of the service brake fails. It comes in **automatically**, works through the circuit still intact, acts on **at least one pair of wheels**, and is therefore **weaker** than the service brake. It has no control of its own.
- The **parking brake** (*freno di stazionamento*) is **mechanical**. It holds a stopped vehicle, including in an emergency, and it must hold on a **slope**.
- The parking brake is **not** used to slow a moving vehicle, not even partly engaged on a steep descent. The one exception is a **complete failure** of the service brake.
- The parking brake acts on **some wheels only**, with no balance between them and no ABS, which is why it brakes a moving vehicle badly.
- **Not every parking brake is a hand lever.** Some are **electric**, some are **pedal-operated**, and some vehicles have none at all, motorcycles among them.

> **For US drivers.** In American usage the parking brake is also called the emergency brake, and the two names refer to one lever. The Italian *freno di soccorso* is not that lever, despite the similar name. It is the second of the three brakes above, the braking that the intact circuit of the foot brake still provides after a partial failure. A car therefore has three brakes in the legal sense and two controls, the pedal and the parking brake. Where a statement says *freno di stazionamento*, the American emergency brake is meant. Where it says *freno di soccorso*, the back-up function of the foot brake is meant.

### Using the brakes on the road

- **Engine braking** (*freno motore*) is strongest in **first gear**, so on a **long, steep descent** use a low gear and the brakes will not **overheat and fade**.
- Never coast in **neutral** or with the **engine off** to save fuel. Power brakes and power steering both need the engine, and the brakes left on their own overheat.
- Brakes work by turning the vehicle's **kinetic energy into heat** through friction. The **linings** are the part the heat punishes most, so long repeated braking weakens them and the braking fades.
- **Power brakes** (*servofreno*) are **common on light vehicles**. They multiply the force of your foot using engine vacuum, so they **stop working with the engine off**, whatever the ignition key is doing, and the pedal turns rock-hard.
- With the wheels **fully locked** the vehicle **no longer steers**.
- **ABS** keeps the wheels from **locking**, which is what makes the braking safer.
- A wheel that still turns keeps answering the steering, so ABS **lets you correct your line** while braking hard.
- ABS lets the tire use the **maximum grip available** while braking.
- ABS acts on **every** wheel, each time on whichever is about to lock.
- ABS works on a **wet road** and with **worn tires**.
- When ABS comes in during an emergency stop, **keep pressing the pedal firmly** rather than easing off.
- In an emergency stop, never use **reverse gear**.

### Checks and maintenance

- The brake circuit is **hydraulic** on cars and on motorcycles alike, and the fluid is what carries the force from the pedal or the lever to the wheels.
- Check the level of the **brake fluid** periodically, on every vehicle. The level falls as the **pads wear**.
- **Test the brakes after washing the vehicle.**
- Brake pads are changed by a **workshop**, not by the driver.

### When braking is weak or pulls to one side

- **Unbalanced or weak braking** comes from **air or vapor** in the hydraulic circuit, **worn linings**, **unevenly worn** drums or discs, **different tire pressures on the same axle**, **overheated linings**, repeated heavy braking, or a load that is **too heavy or badly distributed**.
- Unbalanced brakes show themselves three ways: only the wheels on **one side** lock, the vehicle **swerves toward the wheel that locks first**, and the treads wear **unevenly**.
- Weak braking is **not** caused by a worn parking brake, by worn steering parts, by poorly lubricated drums or discs, by clutch-pedal play, by power steering on a small engine, by disc brakes on the rear axle, by winter tires, or by running on methane, and unbalanced brakes never show up as overheated engine **coolant**.

## Tires

- Check pressure **periodically** and **cold**, including the **spare**.
- **Under-inflation** causes **edge wear**, more friction and higher consumption, heavy steering, and less stability. Tires therefore run coolest at the pressure the **manufacturer** recommends.
- **Over-inflation** wears the **center** of the tread and reduces grip.
- **Different pressures on the same axle** make the car pull, skid in curves, and brake unevenly.
- Grip and stability depend on the pressure, so set **every wheel** to the figure the **manufacturer** recommends, adjusted for the **load** carried. That figure follows the load, not the material of the rims.
- A trailer's tires take the pressure set for the **trailer's own load**, which may differ from the towing vehicle's.
- Check the **sides** of the tires as well, where a cut or a bulge can end in a sudden blowout or deflation.
- A **tire-pressure monitoring system** (TPMS) adds safety.
- The maker's table gives a **normal** figure and a higher **laden** figure, so the correct pressure depends on the **load and the number of people carried**. Set the laden figure **before** a trip with the seats full or the trunk packed, and go back to the normal one afterwards. It does not mean adding air each time a passenger gets in.
- The pressure for a long journey is the **maker's figure for the load** carried, the same as for any other trip.
- Minimum tread depth is **1.6 mm for cars** and **1.0 mm for motorcycles**. Tires on the **same axle must be identical**, and the size must match the vehicle's approval.
- **Winter tires** (*pneumatici invernali*) go on **all** wheels, and they carry no special lower speed limit.
- **Studded tires** (*pneumatici chiodati*) may be used only in the allowed season, and they too go on **all** wheels, never on two only.
- **Snow chains** (*catene da neve*) must be an **approved type**. Using non-approved chains is penalized as if you carried none.
- Chains go on the **drive wheels**. On a **4x4** that means all four, not the rear pair.
- Use chains only on a **snow-covered** road. On snow-free stretches they damage the suspension.
- A **tubeless** tire **deflates slowly** when punctured, so the car holds its direction. A tire **with an inner tube** goes down fast instead.
- With a nail in a tubeless tire you may **drive on carefully** and stop as soon as you can to have it repaired.
- **Leave the nail where it is** until the repair. Pulling it out opens the hole and lets the air escape.
- Have the puncture repaired properly. A **sealant can** is one way of doing it, not the only one.
- Tires may be **rotated** periodically to even out wear.
- Tires should be **replaced after several years even if not worn**.
- **Nitrogen-filled** tires use the **same pressure** as air-filled ones.
- A **space-saver spare** has a **low speed limit**, about 80 km/h. Passengers may still be carried while it is fitted.
- To change a wheel, park on **level, stable ground**, set the **parking brake** and a gear, get passengers **off the carriageway**, loosen the bolts slightly **before** jacking, never get **under** the jacked car, and fully tighten **after** lowering it.
- The jack goes **only at the lifting points the manufacturer marks** under the body, close to the wheel being changed. Any other point of the side member is the wrong answer, and so is the point farthest from the wheel.

## Suspension and shock absorbers

- A suspension sits between the **frame** and the wheel, and every wheel has one, front and rear alike.
- Suspension keeps the **wheels on the road** and absorbs the bumps the surface sends up, so it aids both **comfort and safety**.
- The suspension works on a **straight road** as well as in curves, because a rough surface sends up bumps everywhere.
- By keeping the wheels pressed to the road, suspension and shock absorbers shape how the vehicle answers the **steering**, so the precision of the steering depends on their condition.
- Suspension becomes inefficient through **wear** or after suffering **strong impacts**. Its elastic parts absorb blows, and heavy ones damage them all the same.
- **Overloading** makes the suspension temporarily inefficient, wears it rapidly when it is repeated, and can break it outright.
- The remedy for an overload is to **reduce the load**, because raising the tire pressure leaves the excess weight on the suspension and the shock absorbers.
- A vehicle with inefficient suspension loses **road-holding** and **comfort**, and it tires the driver more. The **aim of the low beams** can go wrong as well. The failure of a single suspension is enough to bring these effects on.
- Suspension and shock absorbers are replaced when wear or damage calls for it, rather than at a fixed mileage. They need checks and maintenance throughout the vehicle's **warranty**, and sealed-circuit shock absorbers need them too.
- The **shock absorbers** damp the oscillations of the suspension, and by holding the wheel against the road they contribute to **road-holding**. A vehicle carries suspension and shock absorbers together, each doing its own part.
- **Overloading** makes the shock absorbers inefficient and wears them out early, whatever the driving style, because the excess weight itself is what overworks them.
- The stiffness of the shock absorbers is adjusted in a **specialist workshop**, with equipment the owner of the vehicle does not have.
- Worn shock absorbers are replaced with new **shock absorbers**, which is what restores the suspension's proper working.
- Worn shock absorbers make the vehicle behave abnormally in **braking** and above all **in curves**, and they worsen its **road-holding**.
- Worn shock absorbers wear the tire tread **unevenly** and raise the risk of breaking the suspension **springs**.
- Worn shock absorbers let the body go on bouncing after each bump, so ride **comfort** drops for the passengers.

## Steering

- Check the **play** in the steering. Excessive play makes the line imprecise.
- **Vibration** in the steering suggests the front wheels need **balancing**.
- Wheel **alignment (toe)** affects steering precision.
- **Power steering needs the engine running.**
- If the power steering fails, the steering goes **heavy**. A failure shows as **heavier** steering, never as easier steering.
- Heavy steering can also mean low tire pressure.
- A **puncture pulls** the steering toward the deflated wheel.
- Power steering helps the driver keep control when a tire is punctured.
- Power steering does **not** improve braking.
- Hold the wheel **at the sides**, at about **9 and 3** on a clock, never low with the hands **under the spokes**, and remember many steering wheels **adjust for height**.

## Fire, visibility, and the cabin

- In a **vehicle fire**, turn the **ignition key off** to cut the electrical system.
- With no extinguisher, throw **sand or earth at the base of the flames** or smother them with a **wet blanket**.
- Never try to **empty or remove the fuel tank** of a burning vehicle, LPG included.
- The **inertial switch** (*interruttore inerziale*) is a safety device fitted to some vehicles. Its name comes from inertia, the tendency of a moving body to keep moving, and a crash is the moment when the vehicle stops abruptly while everything in it is still moving forward. The switch senses that violent deceleration and at once cuts the flow of fuel to the engine. A crash can break fuel lines and cause sparks, and fuel that keeps flowing is what feeds a fire, so the switch **reduces** the fire risk.
- Keep the glass **clean and transparent**, which gives the driver better visibility outside.
- Check the **wiper blades** and replace them when they are worn.
- Keep the **washer fluid** reservoir topped up.
- **Stickers and hanging objects** reduce visibility. Applying **adhesive film** to the windshield and to the front side windows is prohibited, whether or not the film can be peeled off later.
- A **cracked windshield is replaced**, never taped over.
- Dirt and **dust** on the outside of the glass call for the washer and wipers rather than the **defogger** (the *demister*: warm air that clears condensation from the inside of the glass). Water that the vehicle ahead throws up onto the windshield on a wet road is cleared the same way, with the washer and the wipers.
- The **air conditioning also defrosts** the windshield quickly in winter.
- **In the cabin.** Keep nothing loose **under the driver's seat**, switch on the **child locks** with children aboard, set the **navigator before moving off**, and use the **phone only with hands-free**, never to text.

## Variable-message signs

- A **variable-message sign**, the electronic panel over an autostrada, carries the **same legal force as a fixed sign**. It is not limited to warning of danger: it can impose an obligation and it can set a prohibition.

## The exhaust system

- The exhaust carries gases away after **reducing their toxicity, pressure, and temperature**, and it **lowers noise**.
- A **deteriorated muffler** raises **noise pollution**.
- A deteriorated muffler is replaced with an **approved** type for that vehicle.
- The exhaust is replaced at a **workshop**.
- A holed pipe is never patched with glass wool and tape.
- The exhaust system is not replaced at every oil change.
- Modifying or tampering with the exhaust system is punishable even in town. A vehicle is driven only with a working muffler, the *silenziatore*, on roads inside town and outside it alike.
- Electric vehicles have no exhaust to maintain.

## Motorcycle-specific checks

- On most motorcycles the hands do much of the work that a car driver's feet do. The right hand turns the throttle grip and pulls the front brake lever, and the left hand pulls the clutch lever, while the left foot shifts gears and the right foot works the rear brake. So a rider's hands stay on the handlebar whenever the motorcycle is moving, and also when it is held still on a slope with the brakes.
- The **emergency (kill) switch** is a small switch on the handlebar, usually beside the right grip where the thumb can reach it. It stops the engine at once, **without taking the hands off the bars**. This matters most when you stop on a steep slope, because both hands are holding the brake levers and you cannot let go to reach the key.
- The switch is also there for a **stuck throttle**, when the grip stays open after you release it. If twisting the grip back and forth does not free it, the rider uses the switch and pulls in the clutch at the same time, which removes power from the rear wheel, and then leaves the road and stops.
- The engine starts only with the emergency switch set to ON or Run. If you stopped the engine with the switch, move it back to ON or Run before you try to start again.
- The emergency switch sits **on the handlebar**, not on a pedal, the side stand, or the gear lever.
- The emergency switch is **not** a parking brake, a wheel lock, or an anti-theft device.
- For **ordinary stops, prefer the ignition key**. The key switches the vehicle off and comes out with you, while the emergency switch is meant for stopping the engine quickly without letting go of the bars.
- If the emergency switch fails, have it **repaired promptly**.
- Check the **transmission chain's** tension, lubrication, and wear. A chain left unlubricated wears quickly and can snap.
- A chain that snaps can **lock the rear wheel** and cause loss of control.
- A worn chain is **replaced**, never reinforced with wire.
- Often the **front and rear sprockets** go with the chain when it is replaced.
- The transmission chain connects the **front sprocket** on the engine to the **rear sprocket** on the wheel, and that link is how the drive reaches the wheel. New sprockets keep the vehicle's original transmission ratio.
- A motorcycle's **engine oil** is checked with the bike **upright on its wheels**, never on the side stand, on **level ground**, and a few minutes after the engine has been switched **off**. Upright means vertical, held by hand with both wheels on the ground, because on the side stand the bike leans and the oil gathers on one side.
- Some motorcycle engines show the oil level through a **small window on the sump**.
- A motorcycle has levels to check periodically like any vehicle, which are the **engine oil** and the **brake fluid** in its **transparent reservoir**.
- An **air-cooled** motorcycle has **no coolant** to check. Only a water-cooled one does.

## Summary of key points

1. **Grip** is higher on rough, dry surfaces and lower when wet or oily, or on rails, markings, and manholes. Low grip means **longer braking** and skids.
2. In a curve, the outward force **grows with speed**. **High or unsecured loads, a narrow track, and a tight radius** favor rollover.
3. Use a **low gear on long descents** to avoid brake fade. With **ABS, keep the pedal pressed**. **Power brakes need the engine**, and the parking brake is **not** for normal braking.
4. For tires, check them **cold**, including the spare, with tread of **1.6 mm for a car and 1.0 mm for a motorcycle**, identical tires on the same axle, winter tires on all wheels, and approved chains.
5. **Worn suspension or shock absorbers** ruin road-holding and wear tires unevenly. **Power steering needs the engine**, and a puncture **pulls** toward the flat tire.
6. The **exhaust** cuts toxicity, pressure, temperature, and noise. On a motorcycle, check the **kill switch, chain, oil (upright), and brake fluid**.
7. In a **fire**, turn the key off and smother the flames with sand, earth, or a wet blanket. Never touch the fuel tank. Keep the **glass clean**, replace a **cracked windshield**, set the **navigator before moving**, and use the **phone only hands-free**.
Elementi costitutivi del veicolo importa.it:
## Cosa copre questo argomento

Le parti del veicolo che ti tengono al sicuro e come mantenerle: **aderenza e tenuta di strada, freni (e ABS, il sistema antibloccaggio), pneumatici, sospensioni e ammortizzatori, sterzo, scarico**, più alcuni controlli **specifici della moto**. Molte domande riguardano causa ed effetto, cioè cosa fanno al comportamento del veicolo i componenti usurati o sbagliati.

## Aderenza e tenuta di strada

- L'**aderenza** permette alle ruote di trainare, sterzare e mantenere la traiettoria. Si oppone anche allo slittamento dello pneumatico sull'asfalto, qualunque sia la forza che lo spinge lateralmente.
- L'aderenza è **maggiore su asfalto ruvido, asciutto e pulito** e **minore su superfici bagnate, unte o segnate**. Tutto ciò che si frappone tra pneumatico e asfalto la riduce, foglie, ghiaccio e fango compresi.
- Quando l'aderenza cala, lo **spazio di frenata cresce** e le **frenate brusche** diventano pericolose.
- Quando l'aderenza cala, le ruote possono **slittare**, soprattutto in curva, e le ruote motrici possono **pattinare**.
- Dove l'aderenza è scarsa, la **velocità va ridotta**, su ogni tipo di strada e non solo in curva. L'aderenza scarsa limita anche la velocità alla quale una curva può essere percorsa in sicurezza.
- L'aderenza è nettamente minore su **rotaie del tram, segnaletica orizzontale e tombini bagnati**, cosa che conta per le moto. L'aderenza di una moto dipende dal **tipo di pavimentazione stradale** che sta attraversando.

## Curve: slittamento e ribaltamento

- In curva una forza spinge il veicolo **verso l'esterno** e **cresce con la velocità**.
- Troppa velocità può causare uno **slittamento** o un **ribaltamento**.
- Il ribaltamento è reso più probabile da un **carico alto o non assicurato**, da una **carreggiata stretta** con le ruote ravvicinate e da una **curva stretta** con raggio piccolo.

## Freni e ABS

### I tre freni

La legge italiana distingue **tre freni**. Sono tre funzioni frenanti, non tre comandi: una rallenta e ferma il veicolo in marcia, una lo ferma quando la prima si guasta e una lo tiene fermo in sosta. Due parole descrivono come un freno trasmette la forza, e i punti qui sotto usano entrambe: un freno **idraulico** la trasmette con un liquido in un circuito chiuso, un freno **meccanico** con un'asta, un cavo o un leveraggio.

- Il **freno di servizio** è il pedale. Rallenta e ferma il veicolo in marcia, è **idraulico** ed è costruito su **due circuiti separati**, così un singolo guasto ne disattiva solo una parte.
- Il **freno di soccorso** è la frenatura che resta quando una parte del freno di servizio si guasta. Entra in funzione **automaticamente**, lavora attraverso il circuito rimasto integro, agisce su **almeno una coppia di ruote** ed è quindi **meno efficace** del freno di servizio. Non ha un comando proprio.
- Il **freno di stazionamento** è **meccanico**. Tiene fermo il veicolo in sosta, anche in situazioni di emergenza, e deve tenere anche in **pendenza**.
- Il freno di stazionamento **non** si usa per rallentare un veicolo in movimento, nemmeno inserito parzialmente in una discesa ripida. L'unica eccezione è l'**avaria completa** del freno di servizio.
- Il freno di stazionamento agisce **solo su alcune ruote**, senza ripartizione tra loro e senza ABS, ed è per questo che frena male un veicolo in movimento.
- **Non tutti i freni di stazionamento sono a leva manuale.** Alcuni sono **elettrici**, altri **a pedale**, e alcuni veicoli non ne hanno affatto, tra questi i motocicli.

### Usare i freni su strada

- Il **freno motore** è massimo con la **prima marcia**, quindi su una **discesa lunga e ripida** usa una marcia bassa e i freni non **surriscalderanno né perderanno efficacia**.
- Non scendere mai in **folle** o a **motore spento** per risparmiare carburante. Servofreno e servosterzo hanno bisogno del motore, e i freni lasciati soli si surriscaldano.
- I freni trasformano l'**energia cinetica in calore** per attrito. Le **guarnizioni frenanti** sono la parte più sollecitata dal calore, quindi frenate lunghe e ripetute le indeboliscono e la frenata perde efficacia.
- Il **servofreno** è **diffuso sui veicoli leggeri**. Moltiplica la forza del piede usando la depressione del motore, quindi **non funziona a motore spento**, qualunque cosa faccia la chiave di accensione, e il pedale diventa durissimo.
- Con le ruote **completamente bloccate** il veicolo **non sterza più**.
- L'**ABS** impedisce alle ruote di **bloccarsi**, ed è questo che rende la frenata più sicura.
- Una ruota che continua a girare risponde ancora allo sterzo, quindi l'ABS **permette di correggere la traiettoria** anche in frenata decisa.
- L'ABS consente allo pneumatico di sfruttare la **massima forza aderente** in frenata.
- L'ABS agisce su **tutte** le ruote, di volta in volta su quella che sta per bloccarsi.
- L'ABS funziona anche su **strada bagnata** e con **pneumatici usurati**.
- Quando l'ABS entra in azione in un arresto d'emergenza, **continua a premere il pedale con decisione** invece di alleggerire.
- In una frenata d'emergenza non si inserisce mai la **retromarcia**.

### Controlli e manutenzione

- Il circuito frenante è **idraulico** sia sulle auto sia sui motocicli, e il liquido è ciò che trasmette alle ruote la forza del pedale o della leva.
- Controlla periodicamente il livello del **liquido dei freni**, su ogni veicolo. Il livello cala con l'**usura delle pastiglie**.
- **Prova i freni dopo il lavaggio del veicolo.**
- Le pastiglie si cambiano in **officina**, non dal conducente.

### Quando la frenata è debole o tira da un lato

- Una **frenata squilibrata o debole** deriva da **aria o vapore** nel circuito idraulico, **guarnizioni consumate**, tamburi o dischi **consumati irregolarmente**, **pressioni diverse degli pneumatici sullo stesso asse**, **guarnizioni surriscaldate**, frenate ripetute e violente, o un carico **eccessivo o mal ripartito**.
- I freni squilibrati si manifestano in tre modi: si bloccano solo le ruote di **un lato**, il veicolo **sbanda verso la ruota che si blocca per prima** e i battistrada si consumano in modo **irregolare**.
- La frenata debole **non** è causata da un freno di stazionamento usurato, da organi dello sterzo consumati, da tamburi o dischi poco lubrificati, dal gioco del pedale della frizione, dal servosterzo su un veicolo di piccola cilindrata, da freni a disco sull'asse posteriore, da pneumatici invernali, né dall'alimentazione a metano, e i freni squilibrati non si manifestano mai con il surriscaldamento del **liquido di raffreddamento**.

## Pneumatici

- Controlla la pressione **periodicamente** e **a freddo**, compresa la **ruota di scorta**.
- La **bassa pressione** causa **usura sui bordi**, più attrito e consumi più alti, sterzo pesante e minore stabilità. Gli pneumatici quindi restano più freschi alla pressione consigliata dal **costruttore**.
- La **pressione eccessiva** consuma il **centro** del battistrada e riduce l'aderenza.
- **Pressioni diverse sullo stesso asse** fanno tirare l'auto, slittare in curva e frenare in modo squilibrato.
- L'aderenza e la stabilità dipendono dalla pressione, quindi regola la pressione di **ogni ruota** sul valore consigliato dal **costruttore**, adeguato al **carico** trasportato. Quel valore dipende dal carico, non dal materiale dei cerchioni.
- Gli pneumatici del rimorchio prendono la pressione prevista per il **carico del rimorchio**, che può essere diversa da quella della motrice.
- Controlla anche i **fianchi** degli pneumatici, dove un taglio o un rigonfiamento può provocare improvvisi scoppi o sgonfiamenti.
- Il **sistema di rilevamento della pressione** (TPMS) aumenta la sicurezza.
- La tabella del costruttore dà un valore **normale** e uno più alto **a pieno carico**, quindi la pressione corretta dipende dal **carico e dal numero di persone trasportate**. Imposta il valore a pieno carico **prima** di un viaggio con i sedili occupati o il bagagliaio pieno, e torna a quello normale dopo. Non significa aggiungere aria ogni volta che sale un passeggero.
- Per un viaggio lungo la pressione è quella **del costruttore per il carico** trasportato, come per qualsiasi altro viaggio.
- La profondità minima del battistrada è di **1,6 mm per le auto** e **1,0 mm per i motocicli**. Gli pneumatici sullo **stesso asse devono essere identici**, e la misura deve corrispondere all'omologazione del veicolo.
- Gli **pneumatici invernali** vanno su **tutte** le ruote e non hanno speciali limiti di velocità inferiori.
- Gli pneumatici **chiodati** si usano solo nella stagione consentita e anch'essi vanno su **tutte** le ruote, mai solo su due.
- Le **catene da neve** devono essere di **tipo omologato**. Usare catene non omologate è sanzionato come se non ne avessi.
- Le catene vanno sulle **ruote motrici**. Su un **4x4** questo significa tutte e quattro, non solo le posteriori.
- Usa le catene solo con **strada innevata**. Sui tratti privi di neve danneggiano le sospensioni.
- Uno pneumatico **tubeless** si **sgonfia lentamente** se forato, così il veicolo mantiene la direzione. Uno pneumatico **con camera d'aria** si sgonfia invece rapidamente.
- Con un chiodo conficcato in uno pneumatico tubeless puoi **proseguire con cautela** e fermarti appena possibile per farlo riparare.
- **Lascia il chiodo dov'è** fino alla riparazione. Estrarlo apre il foro e fa uscire l'aria.
- Fai riparare la foratura a regola d'arte. La **bomboletta sigillante** è uno dei modi, non l'unico.
- Gli pneumatici possono essere **ruotati** periodicamente per uniformare l'usura.
- Gli pneumatici vanno **sostituiti dopo alcuni anni anche se non consumati**.
- Gli pneumatici **gonfiati con azoto** usano la **stessa pressione** di quelli ad aria.
- Il **ruotino di scorta** ha un **limite di velocità basso**, circa 80 km/h. Con il ruotino montato si possono comunque trasportare passeggeri.
- Per cambiare una ruota, parcheggia su **terreno piano e stabile**, inserisci il **freno di stazionamento** e una marcia, fai scendere i passeggeri **fuori della carreggiata**, allenta leggermente i bulloni **prima** di sollevare con il cric, non andare mai **sotto** l'auto sollevata e serra a fondo **dopo** averla riabbassata.
- Il cric va messo **solo nei punti di sollevamento indicati dal costruttore** sotto la scocca, vicino alla ruota da sostituire. Qualunque altro punto del longherone è la risposta sbagliata, e lo è anche il punto più lontano dalla ruota.

## Sospensioni e ammortizzatori

- Una sospensione sta tra il **telaio** e la ruota, e ogni ruota ha la sua, davanti come dietro.
- Le sospensioni tengono le **ruote sulla strada** e assorbono le asperità che il fondo trasmette, quindi contribuiscono sia al **comfort sia alla sicurezza**.
- Le sospensioni lavorano anche in **rettilineo**, oltre che in curva, perché un fondo irregolare trasmette asperità ovunque.
- Tenendo le ruote aderenti alla strada, sospensioni e ammortizzatori determinano come il veicolo risponde allo **sterzo**, quindi la precisione della sterzata dipende dalle loro condizioni.
- Le sospensioni diventano inefficienti per **usura** o dopo aver subito **urti troppo forti**. Le loro parti elastiche assorbono i colpi, e quelli violenti le danneggiano ugualmente.
- Il **sovraccarico** rende le sospensioni temporaneamente inefficienti, se ripetuto le consuma rapidamente e può arrivare a romperle.
- Il rimedio al sovraccarico è **ridurre il carico**, perché aumentare la pressione degli pneumatici lascia comunque il peso in eccesso su sospensioni e ammortizzatori.
- Un veicolo con sospensioni inefficienti perde **tenuta di strada** e **comfort**, e affatica di più il conducente. Può sballarsi anche l'**assetto dei proiettori anabbaglianti**. La rottura di una sola sospensione basta a produrre questi effetti.
- Sospensioni e ammortizzatori si sostituiscono quando l'usura o un danno lo richiedono, non a un chilometraggio fisso. Richiedono verifiche e manutenzione per tutta la **garanzia** del veicolo, e ne hanno bisogno anche gli ammortizzatori a circuito sigillato.
- Gli **ammortizzatori** smorzano le oscillazioni delle sospensioni e, tenendo la ruota a contatto con la strada, contribuiscono alla **tenuta di strada**. Un veicolo ha sospensioni e ammortizzatori insieme, ciascuno con il proprio compito.
- Il **sovraccarico** rende inefficienti gli ammortizzatori e li consuma precocemente, qualunque sia lo stile di guida, perché è il peso in eccesso a sollecitarli oltre misura.
- La rigidità degli ammortizzatori si regola in **officina specializzata**, con attrezzature che il proprietario del veicolo non ha.
- Gli ammortizzatori usurati si sostituiscono con nuovi **ammortizzatori**, ed è questo che ripristina il corretto funzionamento delle sospensioni.
- Gli ammortizzatori scarichi provocano un comportamento anomalo del veicolo in **frenata** e soprattutto **in curva**, e ne peggiorano la **tenuta di strada**.
- Gli ammortizzatori scarichi provocano un'usura **irregolare** del battistrada e aumentano il rischio di rottura delle **molle** delle sospensioni.
- Con gli ammortizzatori scarichi la carrozzeria continua a oscillare dopo ogni sobbalzo, quindi il **comfort** di marcia dei passeggeri diminuisce.

## Sterzo

- Va controllato il **gioco** dello sterzo. Un gioco eccessivo rende la traiettoria imprecisa.
- Le **vibrazioni** dello sterzo indicano che le ruote anteriori vanno **equilibrate**.
- La **convergenza** delle ruote influisce sulla precisione di guida.
- Il **servosterzo richiede il motore acceso**.
- Se il servosterzo si guasta, lo sterzo diventa **duro**. Un guasto si manifesta con uno sterzo **più duro**, mai più facile.
- Uno sterzo duro può indicare anche una pressione bassa degli pneumatici.
- Una **foratura fa tirare** lo sterzo verso la ruota sgonfia.
- Il servosterzo aiuta a mantenere il controllo quando si fora uno pneumatico.
- Il servosterzo **non** migliora la frenata.
- Impugna il volante **ai lati**, all'incirca alle **ore 9 e 15**, mai in basso con le mani **sotto le razze**, e ricorda che molti volanti sono **regolabili in altezza**.

## Incendio, visibilità e abitacolo

- In caso di **incendio del veicolo**, gira la **chiave di accensione su off** per spegnere l'impianto elettrico.
- Senza estintore, getta **sabbia o terra alla base delle fiamme** o soffocale con una **coperta bagnata**.
- Non tentare mai di **svuotare o smontare il serbatoio** di un veicolo in fiamme, GPL compreso.
- L'**interruttore inerziale** è un dispositivo di sicurezza di cui sono dotati alcuni veicoli. Il nome viene dall'inerzia, la tendenza di un corpo in movimento a continuare a muoversi, e un urto è il momento in cui il veicolo si ferma di colpo mentre tutto ciò che contiene continua ad andare avanti. L'interruttore avverte quella forte decelerazione e blocca subito l'afflusso di carburante al motore. Un urto può rompere i tubi del carburante e provocare scintille, e il carburante che continua a scorrere è ciò che alimenta un incendio, quindi l'interruttore **riduce** il rischio di incendio.
- Tieni i vetri **puliti e trasparenti**, il che garantisce al conducente una migliore visibilità esterna.
- Controlla le **spazzole del tergicristallo** e sostituiscile quando sono consumate.
- Mantieni pieno il serbatoio del **liquido lavacristallo**.
- **Adesivi e oggetti appesi** riducono la visibilità. È vietato applicare **pellicole adesive** sul parabrezza e sui vetri laterali anteriori, che la pellicola sia rimovibile o no.
- Un **parabrezza incrinato si sostituisce**, mai riparato con nastro adesivo.
- Sporco e **polvere** sui vetri richiedono lavacristallo e tergicristalli, non il disappannamento. Anche l'acqua che il veicolo che precede solleva sul parabrezza a strada bagnata si toglie allo stesso modo, con lavacristallo e tergicristalli.
- Il **climatizzatore sbrina** rapidamente il parabrezza anche in inverno.
- **Nell'abitacolo.** Niente oggetti liberi **sotto il sedile del conducente**, **sicura per bambini** inserita con bambini a bordo, **navigatore impostato prima di partire** e **telefono solo con vivavoce**, mai per scrivere messaggi.

## Pannelli a messaggio variabile

- Un **pannello a messaggio variabile**, il pannello elettronico sopra l'autostrada, ha lo **stesso valore prescrittivo di un segnale fisso**. Non si limita a segnalare un pericolo: può imporre un obbligo e può stabilire un divieto.

## L'impianto di scarico

- Lo scarico allontana i gas dopo averne **ridotto tossicità, pressione e temperatura** e ne **abbassa il rumore**.
- Una **marmitta deteriorata** aumenta l'**inquinamento acustico**.
- Una marmitta deteriorata va sostituita con un tipo **omologato** per quel veicolo.
- Lo scarico si sostituisce in **officina**.
- Un tubo forato non si ripara con lana di vetro e nastro.
- L'impianto di scarico non si sostituisce a ogni cambio d'olio.
- Modificare o manomettere l'impianto di scarico è sanzionato anche in città. Un veicolo circola solo con il silenziatore funzionante, sulle strade dentro i centri abitati come fuori.
- I veicoli elettrici non hanno uno scarico da mantenere.

## Controlli specifici della moto

- Sulla maggior parte delle moto le mani fanno gran parte del lavoro che in auto fanno i piedi. La mano destra gira la manopola dell'acceleratore e tira la leva del freno anteriore, la mano sinistra tira la leva della frizione, mentre il piede sinistro cambia le marce e il piede destro aziona il freno posteriore. Così le mani di chi guida restano sul manubrio ogni volta che la moto è in movimento, e anche quando è tenuta ferma in pendenza con i freni.
- L'**interruttore di emergenza (kill switch)** è un piccolo interruttore sul manubrio, di solito accanto alla manopola destra, dove arriva il pollice. Spegne subito il motore, **senza togliere le mani dal manubrio**. Questo conta soprattutto quando ci si ferma su una forte pendenza, perché entrambe le mani tengono le leve dei freni e non si può lasciarle per raggiungere la chiave.
- L'interruttore serve anche in caso di **acceleratore bloccato**, quando la manopola resta aperta dopo averla rilasciata. Se ruotare la manopola avanti e indietro non la sblocca, si usa l'interruttore e insieme si tira la leva della frizione, così la ruota posteriore non riceve più potenza, poi si lascia la strada e ci si ferma.
- Il motore si avvia solo con l'interruttore di emergenza su ON o Run. Se hai spento il motore con l'interruttore, riportalo su ON o Run prima di riavviare.
- L'interruttore di emergenza si trova **sul manubrio**, non su un pedale, sul cavalletto laterale o sulla leva del cambio.
- L'interruttore di emergenza **non** è un freno di stazionamento, un bloccaruote né un antifurto.
- Per le **fermate ordinarie, preferisci la chiave di accensione**. La chiave spegne il veicolo e si porta via con sé, mentre l'interruttore di emergenza serve a spegnere il motore in fretta senza lasciare il manubrio.
- Se l'interruttore di emergenza si guasta, va **riparato al più presto**.
- Controlla tensione, lubrificazione e usura della **catena di trasmissione**. Una catena non lubrificata si consuma rapidamente e può spezzarsi.
- Una catena che si spezza può **bloccare la ruota posteriore** e causare la perdita di controllo.
- Una catena usurata si **sostituisce**, mai rinforzata con filo di ferro.
- Spesso **pignone e corona** si sostituiscono insieme alla catena.
- La catena di trasmissione collega il **pignone** del motore alla **corona** della ruota, e attraverso quel collegamento la spinta del motore arriva alla ruota. Il pignone e la corona nuovi mantengono il rapporto di trasmissione originario del veicolo.
- L'**olio motore** della moto si controlla con il veicolo **in verticale sulle ruote**, mai sul cavalletto, **in piano** e alcuni minuti dopo aver **spento** il motore. In verticale significa dritta, tenuta a mano con entrambe le ruote a terra, perché sul cavalletto laterale la moto pende e l'olio si raccoglie da un lato.
- In alcuni motori di motociclo il livello dell'olio si legge da una **finestrella sulla coppa**.
- Anche la moto ha livelli da controllare periodicamente come ogni veicolo, cioè l'**olio motore** e il **liquido dei freni** nella **vaschetta trasparente**.
- Una moto **raffreddata ad aria** non ha **liquido di raffreddamento** da controllare. Ce l'ha solo quella raffreddata ad acqua.

## Riepilogo dei punti chiave

1. L'**aderenza** è maggiore su superfici ruvide e asciutte e minore con il bagnato o l'unto, o su rotaie, segnaletica e tombini. Poca aderenza significa **frenata più lunga** e slittamenti.
2. In curva la forza verso l'esterno **cresce con la velocità**. **Carichi alti o non assicurati, carreggiata stretta e raggio stretto** favoriscono il ribaltamento.
3. Usa una **marcia bassa nelle discese lunghe** per evitare la perdita di efficacia dei freni. Con l'**ABS, tieni premuto il pedale**. Il **servofreno richiede il motore**, e il freno di stazionamento **non** serve alla frenata di servizio.
4. Per gli pneumatici, controllali **a freddo**, compresa la scorta, con battistrada di **1,6 mm per l'auto e 1,0 mm per la moto**, pneumatici identici sullo stesso asse, invernali su tutte le ruote e catene omologate.
5. **Sospensioni o ammortizzatori usurati** rovinano la tenuta di strada e usurano gli pneumatici in modo irregolare. Il **servosterzo richiede il motore**, e una foratura **fa tirare** verso la ruota sgonfia.
6. Lo **scarico** riduce tossicità, pressione, temperatura e rumore. Sulla moto, controlla **kill switch, catena, olio (in verticale) e liquido dei freni**.
7. In caso di **incendio**, chiave su off e fiamme soffocate con sabbia, terra o una coperta bagnata. Mai toccare il serbatoio. Tieni i **vetri puliti**, sostituisci un **parabrezza incrinato**, imposta il **navigatore prima di partire** e usa il **telefono solo con vivavoce**.

## The map for this topic

The ministry files three subjects under one heading. Read them as one journey and the pile of rules falls into place: **before you set off** (people, animals, cargo, a trailer), **out on the autostrada**, and **when something goes wrong** (an emergency stop, a breakdown, a spilled load). Around the journey sit two habits of recognition: the **marker panels** that flag special vehicles and loads, and the **mismatched road users** you must allow for, whether slow, light, or huge.

> **For US drivers.** Two obligations with no American counterpart: every car must carry a warning **triangle** and a **hi-vis vest**, and you must use them when stopped on the roadway outside town. And the autostrada's right-hand strip is an **emergency lane**, not a shoulder. Driving or stopping on it outside a genuine breakdown is a serious violation.

## Before you set off: people, animals, cargo

- The **number of seats**, at most nine including the driver, is on the **registration document**. For a truck, too, the number of people it may carry is whatever its registration document states.
- Passengers must not block the driver's view or movement.
- One **animal** may ride free if it is no hindrance.
- **More than one** animal must be caged or behind a net. A leash is **not** enough.
- The **load** must be secured against falling or scattering, must not reduce visibility or hide the **lights, plate, or hand signals**, must not unbalance the vehicle, and must stay within the vehicle's **outline limits**. It must also leave the driver full **freedom of movement** at the controls.
- A load may **never project at the front** of the vehicle.
- At the **rear** a load may project **up to 3/10 of the vehicle's length** if it is indivisible.
- A rear projection is marked by the **red-and-white striped retroreflective panel or panels**, and that panel is the **only** marking allowed for it.
- **Sideways** a load may project at most **30 cm (12 in)** from the position lights. No panel marks a sideways projection, because the limit itself is the safeguard.
- Nothing may **drag** on the ground.
- Whenever the load projects, the driver must take every precaution to avoid danger to other road users.
- On **motorcycles and mopeds** a passenger may ride only if the seat is on the registration and the rider is at least **16 years old**. No passenger may be under **5 years old**, and there is no rule that the passenger be an adult.
- Objects carried on a motorcycle must be firmly secured, must not limit the rider's visibility, and may project at most **50 cm (20 in)** beyond the outline, sideways or lengthwise. The projection is capped, not simply forbidden.

## Towing a trailer
### Hooking up

- A **trailer is a separate vehicle**, with its **own plate** and its **own periodic inspection**. Being a vehicle in its own right, it may be hitched to any suitable towing vehicle.
- A trailer has **its own insurance, which covers it even when it is stationary or detached**. While it is being towed on the road, it is covered by the **same policy as the towing vehicle**.
- The **electrical connection** is required even for light trailers.
- The towing gear must be **type-approved, lubricated, and free of play or cracks**, and worn parts are **replaced, never welded**. The coupling must also allow enough **vertical movement** between car and trailer to absorb their different angles over dips and crests.
- When you are not towing, the part of the hitch projecting beyond the vehicle's **rear outline** must be **withdrawn, removed, or folded back**.
- No towable-mass figure on the registration document means **no towing at all**, and a vehicle may tow **only one** trailer or vehicle.

### Loading it

- Heavy items go **low, near the trailer's axle, centered side-to-side**. They are never piled over the hitch (that overloads the coupling and the car's rear axle and lightens the steering wheels) and never set far behind the axle (that sets the trailer swaying).
- Under braking the load shifts **forward**, under acceleration **backward**, and **liquid surge** in a tank is a major instability cause.
- **No one may ride inside a caravan** in motion.
- The **tongue-jack wheel** is the small swiveling wheel at the trailer's nose, used to move it by hand when unhitched, and it **rides raised**.
- Before setting off, check **lights, mirrors, and the load on the hitch**, whose permitted figure is on the **rating plate** fixed to the hitch. The car must not squat at the back or point its headlights up.

### How it changes the drive

- Towing **lengthens the braking distance**, cuts **acceleration**, heats the engine on climbs, makes the combination **wind-sensitive**, **pushes** the car on descents, and **cuts in** on bends. It follows a wider **swept path**, so watch the right rear wheel at curbs.
- The trailer cuts in because it follows a circle of **smaller radius** than the towing vehicle.
- Towing also raises **fuel consumption**, even at moderate speed.
- Before any maneuver with the trailer hitched, make sure no people or objects are within the combination's turning radius.
- The common **inertia (overrun) brake** works off that push: the slowing car is shoved by the trailer, the coupling compresses, and only then do the trailer's brakes apply. Its braking therefore always **lags an instant** behind the car's.
- Rust can weaken the inertia brake after long disuse.
- If the trailer breaks away, the **safety device applies its parking brake** automatically.
- When you leave a trailer parked, engage the **parking brake** and, on a slope, add **wheel chocks**.
- In town a **detached trailer may not be left parked**, unless signs allow it.
- For a **long layup**, jack the trailer off the ground if you can. If you cannot, raise the tire pressure a little and roll it now and then so the tires do not develop **flat spots**.

### The numbers to memorize

- The **towing ratio** compares the mass of the trailer with the mass of the towing vehicle:

$$ towing ratio = trailer's mass ÷ towing vehicle's mass $$

- A trailer with its own service brake and a mass up to **3.5 t** may reach **1**, and a trailer with **no braking device at all** may reach **0.5**. Both limits apply only within the towable mass on the registration document. The limits depend on the masses alone, whatever braking equipment the car itself carries, ABS included.
- Mirrors may project at most **20 cm (8 in)**.
- A combination **over 7 m (7.7 yd)** must keep to the **two right lanes** on an autostrada with three or more lanes.
- A combination **over 3.5 t** means a **zero** blood-alcohol limit for its driver.
- The rear **speed discs** on the trailer's tail show the combination's maximum speeds, and they are required because a car with a trailer is held to lower limits than usual: **70 km/h (43 mph)** outside towns and **80 km/h (50 mph)** on the autostrada. The trailer's mass does not matter, so a trailer **up to 3.5 t** carries them too, unlike a truck up to 3.5 t.
- **T.A.T.S. trailers** (*Trasporto Attrezzature Turistiche e Sportive*: boat, glider, and similar sport-gear trailers) follow the same rules: the **right-side mirror stays required**, and a boat may protrude at most **30 cm (12 in) per side** beyond the rear position lights. The gear they carry serves leisure only and is never goods for trade.
- Which license a heavy combination needs (B96, BE, C, CE) comes later, in the **Licenses, documents & penalties** review.

## Out on the autostrada
### Who may not enter

The autostrada is closed to bicycles, mopeds and **motorcycles under 150 cm³**, to vehicles that **cannot reach 80 km/h (50 mph)**, to motorcycles with a sidecar under 250 cm³, to agricultural and work machines, to vehicles **without pneumatic tires**, in poor condition, out of inspection or over the size limits, to **pedestrians and animals** except in service or rest areas, and to vehicles with **insecure or scattering loads**. In those areas an animal may move about only if **properly supervised**.

Registered trailers of every kind, horse trailers included, enter with the car that tows them.

The 150 cm³ figure is the measure for a gasoline engine, while an electric motorcycle is measured by power instead and must reach **11 kW**. Since 2021 a motorcycle of at least **120 cm³**, or 6 kW electric, is admitted if the rider is an adult.

A pedestrian may walk the emergency lane only to reach an **SOS** call point.

### Getting on and off

- The **acceleration lane** (*corsia di accelerazione*) **yields** to traffic already on the road.
- To leave, move right in time and use the **deceleration lane** (*corsia di decelerazione*) **from its start**, not from some point further along. In the USA the driver manuals give the same advice, and for the same reason, that slowing in a through lane is what causes the rear-end collision, but there it is advice. Here it is **art. 176** of the Code, an obligation and not a recommendation.
- Signal your lane changes.

### Conduct

- **Low beams** (*anabbaglianti*) are compulsory **even by day**. **Reversing, U-turns, and wrong-way driving are forbidden.**
- **Hitchhiking and giving lifts are forbidden.**
- **Commerce is forbidden unless the road authority has authorized it.**
- **Camping is forbidden outside the areas set aside for it**, and it is confined to the **period** set by the road authority. A statement may list every part of the autostrada, ramps and junctions included, to say where this rule applies, and it still allows camping only in the designated areas.
- In a service area (*area di servizio*), do not leave the vehicle parked **more than 24 hours**.
- On the autostrada and on **main extra-urban roads** (*strade extraurbane principali*), parking is allowed **only in the designated areas**, such as service and rest areas.

## When something goes wrong
### The emergency lane

- Stopping is allowed only for **breakdown or illness**, with no reversing, for the **strictly necessary time and never over 3 hours**, after which the vehicle can be towed away. That is an **emergency halt** (*sosta di emergenza*), never parking: the lane is not a place to leave a car, and the three hours are a ceiling, not an allowance.
- At night or in poor visibility keep the **position and hazard lights** on. If they fail, set out the triangle wearing the vest.
- The triangle is also needed, day or night, when the vehicle cannot be moved onto the emergency lane.
- In a **traffic jam**, do not drive on it, except to **exit**, from the **500 m (545 yd) exit-warning sign** onward. Instead, vehicles in the **right lane move toward the left line** to open a gap for emergency vehicles.
- Never give a stranded motorist a **lift**, and never reverse back to help. Assistance means the people who stop are the danger. Call **112** (the European equivalent of the US 911) or roadside assistance instead.
- Never tow a stranded vehicle yourself. On the autostrada only **authorized recovery vehicles** may tow.

### The warning triangle

- The **triangle** (*triangolo*) is compulsory equipment. Place it **behind** the obstacle at least **50 m (55 yd)** back, and **100 m** on the autostrada, where speeds are higher, and **at least 1 m (1.1 yd) from the edge**, so it is **visible from 100 m (110 yd)**. It goes **in the lane the obstacle occupies**, never on top of the load and never in the lane beside it. If a junction lies within 50 m, put it **wherever it is best seen**. The edge that counts is the **outer edge** of the carriageway, not the line between the two directions of travel. The one case in which a triangle also goes **in the middle of the carriageway** is spilled slippery or dangerous material, described below.
- It is **mandatory outside built-up areas at night** when the rear lights are missing or weak, and **even by day** when the obstacle cannot be seen from **100 m**. Inside built-up areas the triangle obligation does **not** apply. Outside built-up areas at night the triangle is always required for a load that has fallen onto the carriageway, since a load carries no lights of its own.

### The hi-vis vest

- Whenever you step onto the road, **even on the emergency lane or a pull-off**, you must wear an **approved high-visibility vest or shoulder straps** (*bretelle*), outside built-up areas.
- The vest only makes you **seen**, and it protects against nothing else. *Retroreflective* means the fabric bounces headlight beams straight back at their source, so you light up in any approaching driver's own lights.
- The vest is no substitute for the triangle.
- The vest need not be yellow.
- One vest or set of straps on board is enough: there is no rule of one per **seat**, since it is worn by whoever gets out to place the triangle.

### Spilled or fallen loads

If your vehicle or a fallen load blocks the road, **clear the passage** as far as possible and **warn** other traffic.

A broken-down vehicle is pushed off the carriageway or, if that is impossible, placed at its **right edge**. Outside built-up areas, a fallen load or crashed vehicles that cannot be moved are pre-signaled with the **warning triangle**.

For spilled **viscous, flammable, or dangerous** substances, also signal in the middle of the road, give hand signals **on the side the triangle does not cover**, and spread **sand or earth** to restore grip. You do these things yourself at once, without waiting for the road authority to arrive.

Inform the **police** when the obstruction cannot be removed.

### Emergency towing of a broken-down vehicle

Use a **solid, properly signaled connection** (a rope, bar, or cable), and doing without one **costs 2 license points**. This kind of tow is allowed only because the towed vehicle can no longer run, through a breakdown or a missing essential part.

The towed vehicle keeps its **hazard flashers** blinking, and the person steering it must hold a **license**. For the driver of the towing car an ordinary **category B** license is enough.

With the engine off its power steering will be **heavy**, and it stays in **neutral** on its own wheels.

## Marker panels: know them at a glance

These four are easy to confuse, so match each panel to its job.

![Square red-and-white striped panel](domandeb_images/4564.jpeg)

- The **red-and-white striped square** marks a **rear-projecting load**, and it is required whenever the load projects at all, even slightly.
- **Two** panels go side by side across the back if the load spans the full width.
- The panel is never placed on the **side** of the vehicle. A load projecting sideways has no panel of its own and is held to the 30 cm (12 in) limit instead.
- The panel is fixed at the **extremity** of the projecting load, where it stays clearly visible.
- The panel tells drivers behind that the vehicle ends farther back than its outline suggests, so they follow with particular caution.

The same panel can also mark a **towed broken-down vehicle** when its lights fail. Otherwise the towed vehicle keeps its **hazard flashers** blinking.

![Yellow-and-red striped rear marker](domandeb_images/4548.jpeg)

The **yellow-and-red striped** panel is the **rear marking of heavy trucks** over 3.5 t. It identifies the vehicle; it never signals a projecting load. Like every marker panel, it is fixed to the vehicle and travels with it.

![Orange plate with codes 33 and 1203](domandeb_images/4550.jpeg)

The **orange** retroreflective plate marks a vehicle carrying **dangerous goods** (the numbers code the hazard and the substance: 33/1203 is gasoline). Not for projecting loads, not for buses.

![Plain yellow rectangular rear marker](domandeb_images/4549_23945.jpeg)

The **plain yellow rectangle** is the rear marker of **long vehicles**: truck-and-trailer combinations (*autotreni*) and tractor-trailers (*autoarticolati*), fitted at the rear of the trailer.

## Sharing the road: speed, mass, and blind spots

- **Cyclists and mopeds** go slowly, wobble, and are hard to judge: keep a lateral gap and avoid small swerves.
- Many are **very young and inexperienced or elderly**, and an elderly cyclist turns the torso slowly and with difficulty to look behind. A cyclist about to maneuver, especially one riding slowly on an extra-urban road, finds it very hard to judge the approach speed of a motor vehicle, so expect one ahead in your lane to misjudge your speed as it turns left.
- Moped riders are often young and short on experience, so foresee their rashness even when one is riding beside you. Judge the gap to a moped about to turn against your own speed, since that distance is hard to gauge when it brakes sharply to turn into a poorly signed side road.
- **Slow vehicles** (three-wheeled mopeds, tractors) appear on extra-urban roads, and the **speed spread** itself is a **danger factor** (*fattore di pericolo*): the bigger the gap between fast and slow traffic, the more catching-up and overtaking, and every such maneuver is a conflict point. The two terms work as a pair. A *fattore di pericolo* is anything that makes traffic more dangerous, and a **fattore di sicurezza** is anything that makes it safer, which is **not** the American engineering sense of a safety factor as a margin built into a design. Read it as "makes things safer" and the true-or-false answer follows.
- At a regular speed on an extra-urban road, and all the more at a sustained speed within the limits, it is hard to judge the speed of a slowly moving agricultural machine and the time it takes to reach it. For a moped, a left turn is especially dangerous because it must cut across the path of one or more columns of faster vehicles coming up in the same direction.
- A **mass mismatch** works the same way: in a collision the lighter vehicle undergoes the larger velocity change, so the risk lands mostly on its occupants. Traffic of **similar speeds and masses** is safer.
- Trucks, truck-and-trailer combinations, and tractor-trailers that exceed the speed limits are among the highest risks a car or motorcycle driver must weigh.
- A **SUV's height and bumpers** endanger pedestrians, cyclists, and small cars, and can hide a child.
- Rigid **bull bars** are metal tube guards bolted to the front of some SUVs and trucks, like the push bars on some US police cruisers. They make a collision **more** dangerous for whoever is struck, because they concentrate the impact instead of letting the bumper crumple.
- Driving one is particularly demanding in **town**, where it is least suited, and it calls for special care in emergency maneuvers.
- A **truck** has large **front and side blind spots**: it may not see a pedestrian or cyclist just ahead when stopped or moving off.
- Behind an **unstable or projecting load**, increase your distance, warn the driver, and pass only when safe. Braking and turning are the moments an unstable load is most likely to fall, and dangling goods can hide the vehicle's turn signals, so a turn is hard to spot.

## Summary of key points

1. **Before you set off**, the vehicle carries at most **nine seats** (per the registration), animals are caged or netted if there is more than one, and the load is secured and within the outline. The load has **no front projection**, may project **3/10** at the rear with the striped panel, and **30 cm (12 in)** sideways. On two-wheelers there are no passengers under 5 and the projection is capped at **50 cm**.
2. A **trailer** is a separate vehicle, with its own plate, inspection and insurance even when parked. The electrical hookup is required. The load goes **low and centered on the axle**. The towing ratio is **1** for a braked trailer and **0.5** for an unbraked one. Towing lengthens braking, cuts in on bends, and pushes on descents. A combination over 3.5 t means **zero alcohol** for its driver.
3. The **autostrada** is closed to vehicles under 80 km/h and to motorcycles under 150 cm³. **Low beams** are on by day. Reversing and U-turns are forbidden. The acceleration lane **yields**. Lifts, camping and commerce are forbidden. Parking in a service area lasts **24 h** at most.
4. **When something goes wrong**, the emergency lane is only for breakdown or illness, for **3 h** at most, and in a jam it is used only to exit from the **500 m** sign. The **triangle** goes 50 m back and 1 m from the edge, and it must be visible from 100 m away. The **vest** is worn whenever you step out, outside town. An emergency tow uses a solid, signaled link and the hazard flashers.
5. Among the **panels**, the striped square marks a projecting load, the yellow-red stripes mark a heavy truck, the orange plate marks dangerous goods, and the plain yellow one marks a long vehicle.
6. In **sharing** the road, watch cyclists and slow vehicles, because the speed spread is a danger, and remember the mass mismatch, the truck blind spots, and that bull bars make impacts worse.
